# EtherCAT interface

[Home](Home.md) · [Operation](Operation.md) · [Troubleshooting](Troubleshooting.md)

## Integration status

**The checked-in ESI XML does not match the compiled firmware dictionary.** [`slave.xml`](../Libs/SOES_Wrapper/autogenerated/slave.xml) identifies an older `Actuator V1` and maps target position, velocity, torque, and GPIO entries. The compiled [`slave_objectlist.c`](../Libs/SOES_Wrapper/autogenerated/slave_objectlist.c) instead maps the EPM commands and sensors described below. The JSON metadata also differs from the compiled identity values.

Before commissioning, reconcile the master's ESI, actual ESC EEPROM/SII contents, and compiled object dictionary. Do not import the current XML and assume its process layout is correct. The repository does not include a verified regeneration/provisioning workflow for those artifacts. The tables below describe the C dictionary compiled by CMake.

## Stack configuration

SOES runs in polling mode from the 1 kHz control timer. The external ESC is accessed through SPI4 using [`esc_hw.c`](../Libs/SOES_Wrapper/hal/esc_hw.c).

| Setting | Value / behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Mailboxes SM0 / SM1 | Offsets `0x1000` / `0x1200`, each 512 bytes |
| Outputs SM2 | Start `0x1400`; assignment `0x1C12` contains `0x1600` |
| Inputs SM3 | Start `0x1A00`; assignment `0x1C13` contains `0x1A00`–`0x1A06` |
| Max RxPDO / TxPDO storage | 512 bytes each |
| Software watchdog | 100 calls; nominal about 100 ms at the intended polling rate |
| FoE / EoE | Disabled |
| Distributed clocks | No `esc_check_dc_handler`; enabling DC may prevent PREOP → SAFEOP |

The watchdog is a stack counter, not a guaranteed wall-clock deadline. `safeoutput_override` is null and SOES's default `APP_safeoutput()` only invokes that optional hook. **Loss of EtherCAT output service does not implement an application demagnetization or discharge action.** Treat bus state and application FSM state separately.

## Master outputs: RxPDO `0x1600`

Rx and Tx are named from the slave's perspective. Offsets below are byte offsets in the packed EtherCAT process image, not offsets in the C `_Objects` struct.

| Byte offset | Object | Field | Width |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `0x6040:00` | Control word | 16 bits |
| 2 | `0x6060:00` | Operation mode | 8 bits |
| 3 | `0x7000:00` | Magnet command | 8 bits |

Total: **4 bytes**. Keep operation mode at zero: it has object storage, but the controller does not use it to select a behavior or update the mode display.

Magnet command bit 0 requests magnetization, and bit 1 requests demagnetization. Each is detected on its own rising edge. Send zero between requests and allow it to be consumed by the device. Raising both bits from zero cancels both requests in the input callback; do not use `0x03` as a command. See [Operation](Operation.md) for sequencing and pulse lockout.

## Master inputs: TxPDOs

| PDO | Start byte | Size | Mapping order |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0x1A00` | 0 | 10 bytes | Status word, mode display, magnet status, force, temperature |
| `0x1A01` | 10 | 20 bytes | Gyro X/Y/Z; linear acceleration X/Y/Z; quaternion R/I/J/K |
| `0x1A02` | 30 | 128 bytes | 64 signed 16-bit ToF distances |
| `0x1A03` | 158 | 64 bytes | 64 unsigned 8-bit ToF SNR values |
| `0x1A04` | 222 | 16 bytes | Four unsigned 16-bit LDC frequency registers, then four RP registers |
| `0x1A05` | 238 | 24 bytes | Four signed 16-bit Hall X values, then Y, then Z |
| `0x1A06` | 262 | 2 bytes | Unsigned 16-bit capacitor voltage |

Total: **264 bytes**. Decode multi-byte process fields using EtherCAT little-endian representation; do not transmit the raw `_Objects` structure, which has a different layout and may contain padding.

### General status fields

| Byte offset | Object | Format | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `0x6041:00` | 16-bit | Application status word |
| 2 | `0x6061:00` | 8-bit | Mode display; currently not updated by application logic |
| 3 | `0x2000:00` | Unsigned 8-bit | Software magnet status, 0 or 1 |
| 4 | `0x2001:00` | IEEE-754 REAL32 | Filtered empirical force estimate, intended N |
| 8 | `0x2040:01` | Signed 16-bit | Temperature in 0.01 °C |

`Error_Code` is **not** mapped into these PDOs. Read it through SDO `0x603F:00`. It is recalculated in the background callback; later checks can overwrite earlier warnings, so it is not an event history or a general fault bitmask.

## Sensor and parameter objects

| Object | Access | Meaning / current behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0x6090:01`–`:0A` | RO | IMU: gyro XYZ, linear acceleration XYZ, quaternion RIJK, raw signed 16-bit reports |
| `0x60A0:01`–`:40` | RO | ToF distances; pixel `i` uses subindex `i + 1` |
| `0x60A1:01`–`:40` | RO | ToF SNR in the same pixel order |
| `0x60B0:01`–`:04` | RO | Four raw LDC inductance/frequency registers |
| `0x60B0:05`–`:08` | RO | Four raw LDC RP registers |
| `0x60C0:01`–`:04` | RO | Hall X for sensors 0–3 |
| `0x60C0:05`–`:08` | RO | Hall Y for sensors 0–3 |
| `0x60C0:09`–`:0C` | RO | Hall Z for sensors 0–3 |
| `0x60D0:00` | RO | Capacitor voltage, 10 mV per count; default battery mode leaves charger uninitialized |
| `0x2100:01` | RW | Pulse-time storage; not used by pulse generation |
| `0x2100:02` | RW | EPM-number storage, initialized from build-time `EPM_NUMBER`; no persistence hook |
| `0x2101:01`–`:FA` | RW | 250 REAL32 storage elements; beginning is repurposed for Git version bytes at startup |

Sensor units and freshness limitations are discussed in [Sensors and force estimation](Sensors-and-Force-Estimation.md). RW access alone does not imply an implemented calibration or persistence function. Pulse generation uses `MAGNETIZATION_TIME`; force estimation uses constants in `TMAG5273.h`, not these SDO arrays.

## Identity and artifact maintenance

The compiled device name at `0x1008` is `Magnecko EPM Controller`. `0x1009` and `0x100A` default to `1.0`; they are not the generated Git version. The `0x1018` vendor, product, and revision defaults are zero, and serial storage is backed by `Obj.serial`.

Any interface change should keep the C object storage, C dictionary, master configuration, XML/JSON/ESX artifacts, and actual EEPROM image consistent. The ESC read helper has a 128-byte termination buffer while the configured mailbox size is 512 bytes; it lacks an enforced length bound. Verify or fix that path before relying on large mailbox transfers, including large parameter reads.
